claims: The 1991–92 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team featured the Fab Five: Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
The Fab Five were the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach an NCAA title game.
The Fab Five reached NCAA championship games in 1992 and 1993.
The Fab Five reached the NCAA Final Four in 1992.
The Fab Five reached the NCAA Final Four in 1993.
The Fab Five lost the 1992 NCAA title game to Duke.
The Fab Five lost the 1993 NCAA title game to North Carolina.
Juwan Howard was the center of the Fab Five.
Chris Webber was the power forward of the Fab Five.
Ray Jackson was the small forward of the Fab Five.
Jimmy King was the shooting guard of the Fab Five.
Jalen Rose was the point guard of the Fab Five.
The Fab Five wore signature baggy shorts and black socks.
In the 1993 title game, Chris Webber called a timeout when Michigan had none left.
Chris Webber's timeout call in the 1993 title game resulted in a technical foul.
The Ed Martin scandal resulted in the University of Michigan disassociating from the Fab Five players.
The Ed Martin scandal resulted in the University of Michigan removing banners.
In April 2026, the Fab Five reunited for a special TNT Sports Altcast during the Final Four.
